image_asset.title: Triangle Congruence Criteria Diagram
image_asset.caption: Visual breakdown of SSS, SAS, ASA, and RHS triangle congruence conditions.

hotspots.label: SSS Criterion
hotspots.popover_text: Side-Side-Side: Equal 3 side lengths guarantee congruence.

hotspots.label: SAS Criterion
hotspots.popover_text: Side-Angle-Side: Angle MUST be strictly included between equal sides.

hotspots.label: ASA Criterion
hotspots.popover_text: Angle-Side-Angle: Two angles and included side align.

hotspots.label: RHS Criterion
hotspots.popover_text: Right-Hypotenuse-Side: Right angle + Hypotenuse + 1 leg equal.

cards.front_question: What is the mathematical definition of geometric congruence between two plane figures?
cards.back_answer: Two plane figures are congruent if they have the exact same shape and the exact same size, so that one can be superimposed onto the other to fit perfectly without gaps or overlaps.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 1

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: Why does the order o...]
cards.front_question: Why does the order of vertices matter when writing a triangle congruence statement like ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ?
cards.back_answer: The vertex order strictly specifies correspondence between matching vertices (A↔X, B↔Y, C↔Z), matching sides (AB=XY, BC=YZ, AC=XZ), and matching angles (∠A=∠X, ∠B=∠Y, ∠C=∠Z).
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 2

cards.front_question: State the SSS (Side-Side-Side) congruence criterion for triangles.
cards.back_answer: If three sides of one triangle are respectively equal to three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 3

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: What is the key requ...]
cards.front_question: What is the key requirement regarding the angle position in the SAS congruence criterion?
cards.back_answer: The angle must be the INCLUDED angle—strictly located between the two known equal sides. Side-Side-Angle (SSA) does not guarantee congruence.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 4

cards.back_answer: If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one leg of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one leg of the other triangle, the two triangles are congruent.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 5

cards.front_question: Why does the AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle) condition fail to establish congruence between two triangles?
cards.back_answer: AAA guarantees that two triangles have the same shape (similarity), but it does not guarantee that they have the same size (e.g., an equilateral triangle with 1 cm sides and another with 10 cm sides both have 60° angles but are not congruent).
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 6

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: In a paper cut-out s...]
cards.front_question: In a paper cut-out superimposition test, what rigid motions are permitted to align two figures?
cards.back_answer: Translation (sliding), Rotation (turning), and Reflection (flipping) are permitted because rigid motions preserve distance and angle measures without altering size or shape.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 7

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: In ΔABC, if side AB ...]
cards.front_question: In ΔABC, if side AB = AC and ∠A = 50°, calculate the measure of ∠B and ∠C.
cards.back_answer: Since AB = AC, angles opposite to equal sides are equal (∠B = ∠C). Angle sum = 180° ⇒ 50° + 2(∠B) = 180° ⇒ 2(∠B) = 130° ⇒ ∠B = 65° and ∠C = 65°.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 8
